boundary.resolution: Six installed table-library functions operating on ordinary language Tables, not typed byte arrays or a new mapped device. CPU/Memory/base/protected-call chapters supply connected contracts.

registers.resolution: All six source interfaces, actual tail-argument branching, missing/nil/default distinctions, returned values/counts and mutable public dependencies. No additional register bank or per-function reset words.

datapath.resolution: Source procedures cover counted tuple n, floor and positive/negative/zero normalization, inclusive nil-bearing intervals, inherited reads/direct writes, in-place mutation and ordinary/custom comparison. The inherited SETT/rawset refill hold is resolved by f13fad92f and the CPU-owned maintained-length contract; this creates no separate library length rule.

visibility.resolution: Ordered direct writes and surviving earlier effects; retained removed value before shifts, final old-tail deletion and interrupted swaps. No transactional or deferred visibility promise.

timing.resolution: Ordinary instruction work, suffix forwarding, recursion and temporary String costs, data/callback-dependent sort and ordered-prefix prescan; no fixed total service time or arbitrary-input termination/resource guarantee.

interrupts.resolution: CPU and IRQ owner chapters supply delivery, masks and waiting. The six ordinary library routines introduce no additional IRQ control interface or substitute for IRQ synchronization.

faults.resolution: Reached ordinary length/index/assignment/call/allocation operations and original callback errors; no library-authored arity/bounds/invalid-sort errors. Mixed-category default less-than is false, not a newly invented comparison fault.

reset.resolution: BIOS startup installs the shared public table global before cartridge entry. Memory and CPU own startup/reset; no per-function hardware reset or universal global-rebinding recovery promise.

programming.resolution: Short tuple, mutation, range and ordering examples accompany the six Table procedures and their maintained-length dependencies.
